nodes.name: SessionGate.test.tsx

nodes.name: SessionGate.tsx
nodes.summary: Client component that gates the app behind an active Better Auth session, redirecting unauthenticated visitors to /login; renders children untouched in zero-login mode.

nodes.name: SessionGate
nodes.summary: Renders children directly in zero-login mode, otherwise wraps them in AuthedGate to enforce a session.

nodes.name: AuthedGate
nodes.summary: Reads the Better Auth session and redirects to /login when unauthenticated, showing a loading state until the session resolves.

nodes.name: UserMenu.test.tsx
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for UserMenu, verifying the signed-in chip, sign-out flow, and that it renders nothing in zero-login mode or without a session.

nodes.name: UserMenu.tsx
nodes.summary: Top-bar user chip with a sign-out popover for multi-user mode; renders nothing when auth is disabled or no session is loaded.

nodes.name: UserMenu
nodes.summary: No-op wrapper that renders the inner user chip only when multi-user auth is enabled.

nodes.name: UserMenuInner
nodes.summary: Renders the signed-in avatar and a sign-out popover, handling outside-click/Escape dismissal and sign-out navigation.

nodes.name: useChat.test.tsx
nodes.summary: Extensive Vitest suite for the useChat hook, mocking the stream runtime, SDK client, and file APIs to verify submit config, file synchronization, and history revalidation.

nodes.name: agentFiles.ts
nodes.summary: Client library for listing, reading, and writing agent files across three sources — graph state, the SDK store, and the backend artifacts files API — normalizing them into a unified AgentFile shape.

nodes.name: filesApiUrl
nodes.summary: Builds an absolute URL to the backend files API by prefixing the configured deployment URL.

nodes.name: getAgentFileSources
nodes.summary: Returns the store/artifact source configuration for a given graph id from AGENT_FILE_SOURCES.

nodes.name: stateFilesToAgentFiles
nodes.summary: Normalizes the graph state's files map into AgentFile records, coercing string/array/object content shapes into text.

nodes.name: resolveStoreLocation
nodes.summary: Maps a store-relative path to its namespace and key by matching the longest configured path prefix.

nodes.name: fetchStoreFiles
nodes.summary: Lists agent files from the SDK store across configured namespace prefixes, decoding content and last-modified timestamps.

nodes.name: fetchArtifactFiles
nodes.summary: Lists and reads artifact files from the backend /files API for the configured path prefixes.

nodes.name: fetchAgentFiles
nodes.summary: Aggregates and de-duplicates agent files from state, store, and artifact sources into a single sorted list.

nodes.name: writeAgentFile
nodes.summary: Writes an agent file back to its source — an SDK store put, the artifacts files API, or a graph state update.

nodes.name: page.test.tsx
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for the login page, verifying email/password and Google sign-in rendering and redirect-when-authenticated behavior.

nodes.name: client.ts
nodes.summary: Better Auth browser client (same-origin /api/auth) with the JWT plugin; authClient.token() mints the short-lived bearer JWT backend requests carry in multi-user mode.

nodes.name: enabled.ts
nodes.summary: Feature-flag helpers (isAuthEnabled / isGoogleAuthEnabled) reading NEXT_PUBLIC env vars; the central gate that keeps multi-user auth code a no-op in zero-login mode.

nodes.name: isAuthEnabled
nodes.summary: Returns whether multi-user auth is enabled from NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_ENABLED; the central gate for all auth code paths.

nodes.name: isGoogleAuthEnabled
nodes.summary: Returns whether the Google sign-in button is offered, from NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_GOOGLE_ENABLED.

nodes.name: token.ts
nodes.summary: Bearer-token plumbing for multi-user mode: caches and refreshes the Better Auth JWT, injects Authorization headers via the SDK onRequest hook, and provides a 401-retrying authedFetch wrapper.
nodes.languageNotes: Holds module-level cache state with an in-flight promise to de-duplicate concurrent token mints; entirely no-op in zero-login mode.

nodes.name: decodeExpiryMs
nodes.summary: Decodes a JWT's exp claim to epoch milliseconds, falling back to a conservative near-term default on failure.

nodes.name: getBearerToken
nodes.summary: Returns the current bearer token, minting/caching a fresh one via Better Auth and refreshing before expiry; null when auth is off.

nodes.name: authOnRequest
nodes.summary: SDK onRequest hook that injects Authorization: Bearer into every langgraph-sdk request; no-op without a token.

nodes.name: authedFetch
nodes.summary: fetch wrapper for raw /files/* calls that injects the bearer and retries once with a fresh token on a 401.

nodes.name: ChatProvider.test.tsx
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for ChatProvider, verifying it exposes the useChat context to descendants and that useChatContext throws when used outside the provider.

nodes.name: ClientProvider.test.tsx
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for ClientProvider, verifying it constructs a single memoized SDK Client from context and that useClient throws outside the provider.

nodes.name: ClientProvider.tsx
nodes.summary: React context provider that constructs a memoized @langchain/langgraph-sdk Client, wiring the bearer-token onRequest hook so every REST/SSE request carries auth in multi-user mode.

nodes.name: ClientProvider
nodes.summary: Constructs a memoized langgraph-sdk Client with API-key headers and the bearer-token onRequest hook, exposing it via React context.

nodes.name: useClient
nodes.summary: Context hook returning the shared SDK Client; throws if used outside a ClientProvider.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the vendored LangGraph server's Postgres runtime layer; re-exports the checkpoint, database, lifespan, metrics, queue, retry, routes, and store submodules.
nodes.languageNotes: Python package barrel that imports sibling submodules and lists them in __all__ for re-export.

nodes.name: database.py
nodes.summary: Manages the async Postgres connection-pool lifecycle (create/start/stop), health checks, and versioned SQL migration execution for the agent server's persistence layer.
nodes.languageNotes: Falls back to a thread-local AsyncConnectionPool so worker threads without the main-thread pool still obtain connections.

nodes.name: lifespan.py
nodes.summary: ASGI lifespan orchestrator that starts the server's subsystems (Postgres pool, checkpointer, run queue, store TTL sweeper, cron scheduler, gRPC, metrics) in order and tears them down in reverse, with a hard-exit watchdog on shutdown.

nodes.name: long_query_monitor.py
nodes.summary: Background loop that periodically scans pg_stat_activity for long-running queries and logs them, coordinating across workers via a Redis lock and last-scan timestamp.

nodes.name: metrics.py
nodes.summary: Defines the worker-pool metrics data models and a get_metrics helper reporting active/available/max run-queue workers.

nodes.name: migrate.py
nodes.summary: Standalone migration entry point that opens a Postgres pool and applies schema and pgvector-index migrations; used to exercise the Go core server in tests.

nodes.name: queue.py
nodes.summary: The run queue: dispatches queued runs to a pool of background event-loop worker threads, tracks in-flight workers, fires completion webhooks, and coordinates graceful drain on shutdown.

nodes.name: redis.py
nodes.summary: Redis client factory and lifecycle for the runtime, with Redis Cluster pub/sub across slots and a GCP IAM credential provider for authenticated managed Redis.

nodes.name: retry.py
nodes.summary: Provides the retry_db decorator that retries async DB/gRPC operations on transient errors (operational/internal errors, pool timeouts, retryable gRPC status codes, undefined-table races).

nodes.name: routes.py
nodes.summary: Placeholder for the runtime's optional internal HTTP routes hook; currently a no-op stub (get_internal_routes = None).

nodes.name: store.py
nodes.summary: Postgres-backed long-term key/value store (PGSTore) with pgvector index setup and Redis-coordinated TTL sweeping, exposed as a lazily-initialized singleton via Store().

nodes.name: connect
nodes.summary: Async context manager yielding a pooled Postgres connection, transparently opening a thread-local pool for non-main worker threads.

nodes.name: create_pool
nodes.summary: Builds the AsyncConnectionPool from the configured DSN with sizing, timeouts, and per-connection configure/reset hooks.

nodes.name: create_conn
nodes.summary: Opens a single standalone async Postgres connection with JSON serde configured, used outside the pool.

nodes.name: migrate
nodes.summary: Applies pending versioned SQL migrations under a version-tracking table, reading and splitting migration files and recording the highest applied version.

nodes.name: start_pool
nodes.summary: Startup routine that boots Redis, opens the pool, applies store config, and runs migrations under a Redis lock, then launches the pool stats loop.

nodes.name: stop_pool
nodes.summary: Shutdown routine that cancels the stats task, closes the pool (thread-local or global), and stops Redis.

nodes.name: migrate_vector_index
nodes.summary: Sets up the pgvector index by lazily importing the store module and delegating to its vector-index migration.

nodes.name: lifespan
nodes.summary: Async lifespan context manager that brings the full server up (pool, checkpointer, ingestion loop, HTTP/UI, gRPC, metrics, store sweeper, query monitor, run queue, cron) and tears it down in reverse on exit.

nodes.name: queue_with_signal
nodes.summary: Runs the queue worker loop and, on unexpected exit or error, triggers a delayed hard process exit so the container is restarted.

nodes.name: _exit_after_flush
nodes.summary: Schedules a watchdog timer that force-exits the process if graceful shutdown and log flushing do not complete within a timeout.

nodes.name: long_query_monitor_loop
nodes.summary: Periodic loop that, gated by a Redis lock and scan interval, queries active long-running Postgres statements and logs them for observability.

nodes.name: _get_long_running_queries
nodes.summary: Queries pg_stat_activity for statements exceeding a duration threshold and returns normalized, JSON-serializable rows.

nodes.name: get_metrics
nodes.summary: Assembles the worker-pool metrics snapshot (max/active/available workers) from the run queue's worker registry.

nodes.name: migrate_for_tests
nodes.summary: Opens a Postgres pool against the migrations directory and applies schema plus pgvector-index migrations; entry point for exercising the Go core server in tests.

nodes.name: BgLoopRunner
nodes.summary: Runs a dedicated asyncio event loop on its own thread, submitting coroutines to it and draining/closing the pool, store, and gRPC client on context exit.

nodes.name: queue
nodes.summary: Core run-dispatch loop: pulls the next run from Postgres, assigns it a background loop runner, spawns the worker coroutine, tracks in-flight workers and webhooks, and drains everything on shutdown.

nodes.name: shutdown_queue
nodes.summary: Cancels in-flight worker and webhook futures and waits for them to settle within a timeout during queue drain.

nodes.name: stats_loop
nodes.summary: Background loop that periodically reports active/max worker gauges to the metrics reporter.

nodes.name: ClusterPubSub
nodes.summary: Redis Cluster pub/sub connection bound to a single node/slot, managing its connection lifecycle, subscribed channels/patterns, and clean teardown.

nodes.name: _GCPIAMCredentialProvider
nodes.summary: Streaming credential provider that mints and refreshes GCP IAM access tokens (sync and async) for authenticating to managed Redis.

nodes.name: _create_redis_client
nodes.summary: Builds the async Redis (or Cluster) client from the configured URI with retry/backoff and optional IAM auth.

nodes.name: start_redis
nodes.summary: Creates the shared Redis client, verifies connectivity with a ping, and launches the Redis stats loop.

nodes.name: redis_stats
nodes.summary: Collects connection-pool statistics across cluster nodes (or the single client) into a RedisPoolStats snapshot.

nodes.name: get_redis
nodes.summary: Returns the shared async Redis client, lazily creating a per-thread client for non-main worker threads.

nodes.name: get_pubsub
nodes.summary: Async context manager yielding a pub/sub subscribed to the given channels/patterns, routing to the correct cluster node by keyslot when clustered.

nodes.name: retry_db
nodes.summary: Decorator that retries an async DB/gRPC callable up to three times on transient failures (operational/internal errors, retryable gRPC codes, undefined-table races).

nodes.name: PGSTore
nodes.summary: Postgres-backed long-term store subclass that routes cursors through the shared pool, batches grouped operations, and performs Redis-coordinated TTL sweeps.

nodes.name: setup_vector_index
nodes.summary: Runs the pgvector index migrations for the store, applying versioned index-creation SQL and embedding-dimension parameters.

nodes.name: Store
nodes.summary: Factory returning the lazily-initialized store singleton, applying store config and starting the store on first use.

nodes.name: event_streaming.py
nodes.summary: HTTP and WebSocket transport routes for the v2 thread-centric event streaming protocol, exposing an SSE stream endpoint, a JSON command endpoint, and full-duplex WebSocket endpoints scoped to a thread.
nodes.languageNotes: Connections are connection-scoped with no cross-connection server state; SSE delivery dedups via a bounded ring buffer to cover the source/session handoff race.

nodes.name: capabilities.py
nodes.summary: Runtime capability probe that verifies the installed langgraph and langchain-core versions expose the symbols required to serve a Protocol v2 streaming run, failing fast with an actionable error otherwise.

nodes.name: constants.py
nodes.summary: Shared constants for the v2 event streaming layer: the run config key, the replay ring-buffer size, the supported channel set, and the default run stream modes.

nodes.name: event_normalizers.py
nodes.summary: Pure helper functions that normalize raw stream event payloads into protocol shapes, extracting text content, mapping run status to lifecycle status, and coercing updates and interrupt data.

nodes.name: namespace.py
nodes.summary: Namespace helpers for the streaming protocol: build stable lookup keys, strip dynamic segment suffixes, parse event names, and test namespace prefix matches.

nodes.name: service.py
nodes.summary: Defines ThreadRunManager, the thread-scoped orchestrator that owns a bound EventStreamingSession, routes protocol commands, and creates or resumes runs for the v2 SSE and WebSocket transports.

nodes.name: session.py
nodes.summary: Defines EventStreamingSession, the per-run protocol session that normalizes raw upstream stream events into protocol frames while managing a replay buffer, subscriptions, namespace lifecycle, and interrupt handling.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses ContextVars to derive stable, replay-safe protocol event ids from the upstream Go core's Redis-stream entry ids, so client-side dedup survives reconnects and restarts.

nodes.name: state_normalizers.py
nodes.summary: Normalizes LangGraph thread-state payloads into protocol-shaped events, covering message content blocks, tool calls, audio blocks reconstructed from message kwargs, and full state messages.

nodes.name: types.py
nodes.summary: Type barrel that re-exports the langchain_protocol wire types and defines the local Subscription and NamespaceInfo dataclasses used across the event streaming layer.

nodes.name: metrics_datadog.py
nodes.summary: Datadog metrics layer built on OpenTelemetry: defines tiered metric definitions, a tier-filtering OTLP exporter, and the DatadogMetricsReporter singleton with counter, histogram, latency, and gauge instruments.
nodes.languageNotes: The OpenTelemetry SDK import is guarded by a try/except so the module degrades to a no-op reporter when the OTEL packages are absent.

nodes.name: _thread_events
nodes.summary: SSE endpoint handler that validates the EventStreamRequest filter, installs a connection-scoped subscription on a ThreadRunManager, and streams deduplicated protocol events until the thread stream ends.

nodes.name: _thread_command
nodes.summary: JSON request/response handler that parses a single protocol command, dispatches it through a short-lived ThreadRunManager, and returns the command result.

nodes.name: _thread_websocket
nodes.summary: Full-duplex WebSocket handler that binds a ThreadRunManager to the socket, forwards incoming commands, and runs a watchdog that closes the socket when the thread stream completes.

nodes.name: ProtocolV2Capabilities
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass describing whether the runtime satisfies Protocol v2 requirements, listing any missing symbols and rendering an actionable error message.

nodes.name: probe_event_streaming_v2_capabilities
nodes.summary: Probes for the langgraph and langchain-core symbols required to serve a Protocol v2 run and returns a ProtocolV2Capabilities result, memoized via lru_cache.

nodes.name: ProtocolV2UnsupportedError
nodes.summary: Exception raised when the runtime lacks the symbols needed for Protocol v2 streaming, carrying the capabilities detail so callers can return a clear error envelope.

nodes.name: extract_text_content
nodes.summary: Extracts a plain-text string from a message content value that may be a string, a list of content parts, or structured records.

nodes.name: normalize_input_requested_data
nodes.summary: Normalizes raw interrupt payloads into the protocol's input-requested data array.

nodes.name: strip_interrupts_from_values
nodes.summary: Removes interrupt entries from a values payload so interrupts are surfaced only through dedicated input-requested events.

nodes.name: is_prefix_match
nodes.summary: Checks whether a namespace array starts with a given prefix, comparing segments literally and falling back to a dynamic-suffix-stripped comparison.

nodes.name: ThreadRunManager
nodes.summary: Thread-scoped run manager that owns a bound EventStreamingSession, routes protocol commands such as run.start, input.respond, and subscribe/unsubscribe, and creates or resumes runs for the SSE and WebSocket transports.

nodes.name: _checkpoint_id_from_run_start_config
nodes.summary: Extracts the checkpoint id from a run.start runnable config, raising ValueError when the nested configurable structure is malformed.

nodes.name: validate_checkpoint_id_from_runnable_config
nodes.summary: Validates that a run.start config's checkpoint id is a well-formed UUID and returns it as a normalized string.

nodes.name: _multitask_strategy_from_run_start
nodes.summary: Resolves the multitask strategy for a new run from the run.start params, falling back to the default when unset or invalid.

nodes.name: EventStreamingSession
nodes.summary: Per-run protocol session that consumes raw upstream stream events, normalizes them into protocol frames, maintains a bounded replay buffer, tracks subscriptions and namespace lifecycle, and emits lifecycle, interrupt, and tool events.

nodes.name: ResumeGap
nodes.summary: Value type signalling that a reconnect cursor has fallen behind the replay buffer head, triggering a resume_gap protocol error instead of silent truncation.

nodes.name: _synth_event_id
nodes.summary: Derives a stable, replay-safe protocol event id from the current upstream Redis-stream entry id and a per-source envelope counter.

nodes.name: _is_supported_channel
nodes.summary: Returns whether a value is one of the protocol's supported subscription channels; shared by the transport routes and the run manager.

nodes.name: _custom_event_matches
nodes.summary: Determines whether a custom stream event's data name matches a subscription's custom-channel filter.

nodes.name: _coerce_interrupt_requests
nodes.summary: Coerces raw interrupt values into a normalized list of interrupt request records for input-requested events.

nodes.name: normalize_event_streaming_state_payload
nodes.summary: Top-level normalizer that converts a raw LangGraph thread-state payload into the protocol's state-message shape.

nodes.name: normalize_event_streaming_message_content
nodes.summary: Normalizes a message's content and additional_kwargs into protocol content blocks, including audio reconstructed from the kwargs.

nodes.name: normalize_event_streaming_content_block
nodes.summary: Normalizes a single content value into a protocol content block, mapping recognized types and wrapping unknown ones as non-standard blocks.

nodes.name: _normalize_state_message
nodes.summary: Normalizes a single state message record into the protocol shape, resolving its role and type, content blocks, and tool calls.

nodes.name: _normalize_state_tool_calls
nodes.summary: Normalizes a message's tool-call entries into protocol tool-call blocks, deriving each call's identity and arguments.

nodes.name: _normalize_audio_block_from_additional_kwargs
nodes.summary: Reconstructs a protocol audio content block from a message's additional_kwargs, inferring the MIME type from the audio format.

nodes.name: Subscription
nodes.summary: Dataclass representing an active WebSocket subscription within a session: its id, channel set, optional namespace filters, depth, and active flag.

nodes.name: NamespaceInfo
nodes.summary: Dataclass caching lifecycle metadata for a namespace: its segments, status, and derived graph name.

nodes.name: DatadogMetricsReporter
nodes.summary: Singleton reporter that lazily creates OpenTelemetry instruments and records counters, histograms, latencies, and gauges to Datadog, honoring each metric's emitting tier.

nodes.name: _FilteringExporter
nodes.summary: OTLP metric exporter wrapper that drops metrics above the configured emitting tier before delegating export to the underlying exporter.

nodes.name: MetricDef
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass describing a metric's type, name, and emitting tier; the value type for all module-level metric definitions.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker for the gRPC bridge subpackage that exposes Python-side services (checkpointing, encryption) to the Go core server.

nodes.name: server.py
nodes.summary: Standalone asyncio gRPC server running alongside the Starlette HTTP server; registers the checkpointer, encryption, and health servicers so the Go core server can call into Python.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses grpc.aio for a fully async server with a module-global instance and task for shutdown coordination.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Barrel that re-exports the Python gRPC servicer implementations (CheckpointerServicerImpl, EncryptionServicerImpl) for the server to register.

nodes.name: checkpointer.py
nodes.summary: Implements the Checkpointer gRPC service, converting protos to/from LangGraph checkpoint types and delegating persistence (put, list, get, delete, copy, prune) to the Python checkpointer so the Go server can use Python-based checkpoint storage.

nodes.name: encryption.py
nodes.summary: Implements the Encryption gRPC service, recursively encrypting/decrypting JSON payloads with nested-subfield and skip-field handling so the Go server can delegate to Python custom encryption.

nodes.name: queue_entrypoint.py
nodes.summary: Async worker entrypoint that boots the selected queue runtime, runs a Starlette health/metrics sidecar server, and coordinates graceful shutdown on signals or fatal errors.
nodes.languageNotes: Injects truststore into SSL before other imports and drives shutdown via asyncio signal handlers plus task done-callbacks.

nodes.name: errors.py
nodes.summary: Defines server-specific exception types: GraphLoadError (rich user-facing graph-load failure with formatted traceback and hints) and HealthServerStartupError.

nodes.name: network.py
nodes.summary: Host/port normalization helpers reconciling bracketed IPv6 literals, wildcard bind addresses, and healthcheck target/URL hosts across socket and URL contexts.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Dynamically resolves and imports the configured LangGraph runtime edition (inmem or postgres) from LANGGRAPH_RUNTIME_EDITION and aliases its submodules under server.runtime.*.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses importlib.util.find_spec plus sys.modules aliasing for plugin-style, boot-time backend selection.

nodes.name: metrics.py
nodes.summary: Type-checking-only re-export shim surfacing the active runtime edition's metrics API (e.g. get_metrics) under server.runtime.metrics; the real module is aliased at runtime by the package __init__.

nodes.name: start_python_grpc_server
nodes.summary: Creates the asyncio gRPC server, registers the health, checkpointer, and encryption servicers, binds the insecure port, starts serving, and marks the service healthy.

nodes.name: stop_python_grpc_server
nodes.summary: Gracefully stops the running gRPC server within a grace period and cancels its serving task.

nodes.name: wait_until_python_grpc_ready
nodes.summary: Polls the gRPC health endpoint over an insecure channel until the server reports SERVING or a timeout elapses, raising RuntimeError on failure.

nodes.name: run_python_grpc_server
nodes.summary: Convenience coroutine that starts the gRPC server and then serves forever, logging and re-raising fatal errors.

nodes.name: _parse_metadata
nodes.summary: Parses a proto map of string to JSON-encoded bytes into a Python dict, raising ValueError on any invalid JSON value.

nodes.name: _build_encryption_context
nodes.summary: Constructs an SDK EncryptionContext from proto model, field, and metadata inputs for the encryption handlers.

nodes.name: EncryptionServicerImpl
nodes.summary: gRPC servicer that recursively encrypts and decrypts JSON fields, honoring nested-subfield and skip rules, by delegating to the configured encryption instance's JSON encryptor/decryptor.

nodes.name: CheckpointerServicerImpl
nodes.summary: gRPC servicer implementing the full checkpointer contract (Put, PutWrites, GetCapabilities, List, GetTuple, DeleteThread, DeleteForRuns, CopyThread, Prune) by converting protos to/from LangGraph checkpoint types and delegating to the Python checkpointer.

nodes.name: _ensure_port_available
nodes.summary: Resolves the bind host and probes whether the health-server port can be bound, raising HealthServerStartupError on resolution failure or port conflict.

nodes.name: health_and_metrics_server
nodes.summary: Builds and runs a Starlette app exposing /health and /metrics (Prometheus lines plus pool stats) on a uvicorn server, with pre-bind port checks and error propagation.

nodes.name: entrypoint
nodes.summary: Sets up the logging context, combines lifespans, launches the health/metrics sidecar task, and runs the selected runtime entrypoint until cancelled.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Top-level async driver that installs signal handlers, runs the entrypoint and health-server tasks, and coordinates graceful shutdown and process exit codes.

nodes.name: normalize_host
nodes.summary: Strips surrounding brackets from IPv6 host literals so socket bind/connect APIs receive the raw address.

nodes.name: format_hostport
nodes.summary: Formats a host and port into a connection string, bracketing IPv6 literals.

nodes.name: get_healthcheck_target_host
nodes.summary: Maps a wildcard or IPv6-any bind host to a concrete loopback target address for healthchecks.

nodes.name: get_healthcheck_url_host
nodes.summary: Resolves a host into a URL-safe host component, bracketing IPv6 addresses and mapping wildcard binds to localhost.

nodes.name: GraphLoadError
nodes.summary: RuntimeError raised when a user-provided graph fails to load, capturing the spec, cause, formatted exception-only traceback, and helpful hints for structured logs and user display.

nodes.name: HealthServerStartupError
nodes.summary: Exception raised when the health/metrics server fails to start, such as on a port conflict or bind failure.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package entry point for the MCP (Model Context Protocol) server; re-exports the Streamable HTTP routes and documents the stateless, JSON-only transport and the supported protocol versions.
nodes.languageNotes: Python package barrel using __all__ to re-export mcp_routes.

nodes.name: _constants.py
nodes.summary: Defines MCP server constants: supported and latest protocol versions, JSON-RPC error codes, and assistant pagination limits shared across the request handlers.

nodes.name: _handlers.py
nodes.summary: Core MCP request handlers for the Streamable HTTP transport: parses and dispatches JSON-RPC messages (initialize, ping, tools/list, tools/call) and maps each LangGraph assistant to an MCP tool.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses functools.lru_cache for a singleton LangGraph client and asyncio.gather to fetch tool schemas concurrently.

nodes.name: _routes.py
nodes.summary: Declares the /mcp route and its HTTP method dispatcher, routing POST to JSON-RPC handling, DELETE to session termination, and rejecting unsupported methods with 405.

nodes.name: _sanitizers.py
nodes.summary: Helpers that adapt LangGraph assistant schemas for MCP consumption: strips LangChain message type definitions from input schemas and normalizes assistant names into spec-compliant MCP tool names.
nodes.languageNotes: Mutates JSON Schema dicts in place and enforces the MCP tool-name charset (^[a-zA-Z0-9_\-.]{1,128}$) via regex.

nodes.name: handle_delete_request
nodes.summary: Handles HTTP DELETE for MCP session termination, returning 404 because this stateless server keeps no session to terminate.

nodes.name: handle_get_request
nodes.summary: Handles HTTP GET for MCP, returning 405 since server-sent-event streaming is not currently supported.

nodes.name: handle_post_request
nodes.summary: Validates and routes an incoming MCP POST body: checks JSON parsing, the Accept header, and JSON-RPC 2.0 framing, then dispatches requests to the JSON-RPC handler or acknowledges responses and notifications.

nodes.name: is_valid_accept_header
nodes.summary: Checks whether the request Accept header advertises application/json or text/event-stream as required by the MCP Streamable HTTP transport.

nodes.name: create_error_response
nodes.summary: Builds a JSON error Response carrying the given message and HTTP status code.

nodes.name: handle_jsonrpc_request
nodes.summary: Dispatches a JSON-RPC request by method (initialize, ping, tools/list, tools/call) and wraps the result or error in a JSON-RPC 2.0 response envelope.

nodes.name: handle_initialize_request
nodes.summary: Handles the MCP initialize request, negotiating the protocol version with the client and returning server capabilities and identity.

nodes.name: handle_tools_list
nodes.summary: Implements MCP tools/list by paging LangGraph assistants, deduplicating them by normalized name, and concurrently building an MCP tool definition from each assistant's input schema.

nodes.name: handle_tools_call
nodes.summary: Implements MCP tools/call by resolving the tool name to a unique assistant, executing a LangGraph run with the supplied arguments, and returning the run result or a tool error.

nodes.name: handle_mcp_endpoint
nodes.summary: Route handler for /mcp that dispatches on HTTP method to the DELETE, GET, or POST handlers and returns 405 for any other method.

nodes.name: simplify_mcp_schema_inplace
nodes.summary: Strips LangChain message type $defs from a LangGraph assistant input schema in place and collapses message-array properties to a single string field for MCP/LLM consumption.

nodes.name: normalize_name
nodes.summary: Converts an assistant name into a valid MCP tool name by collapsing whitespace to underscores, removing disallowed characters, and truncating to 128 characters.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Public API barrel for the vendored lc_security package, re-exporting the SSRF exception, the policy dataclass, the URL/IP/hostname validators, and the SSRF-safe httpx transport and client factory.

nodes.name: validate_resolved_ip

nodes.name: validate_hostname

nodes.name: 000001_init.up.sql
nodes.summary: Consolidated (squashed) initial migration defining the complete NextRole Agent Server database schema: 11 tables backing LangGraph assistants, threads, runs, checkpoints, cron, and the KV store, plus the btree_gin/ltree/pgvector extensions, indexes, sequences, and foreign keys. Applied once at backend boot under a Redis lock.
nodes.languageNotes: Squashed single-file schema. Run and checkpoint tables intentionally omit foreign keys (write-path lock avoidance, async GC); the run table doubles as a work queue with partial indexes on status='pending'/'running' for index-only queue claims, and thread carries partial expression indexes over metadata->>'owner'/'ls_user_id' for multi-user isolation.

nodes.name: checkpoint_writes
nodes.summary: Stores intermediate checkpoint writes per task keyed by (thread_id, checkpoint_ns, checkpoint_id, task_id, idx). Feeds the LangGraph checkpointer's write path.

nodes.name: ConfigDialog
nodes.summary: Renders the Settings dialog — an appearance section plus Model and Connection field groups — and guards saving on deployment URL and assistant ID being present, trimming blank model overrides to undefined before calling onSave.

nodes.name: server.py
nodes.summary: Assembles and exposes the ASGI `app` for the vendored LangGraph agent server: composes global middleware (private-network, CORS, access logging, request IDs), registers exception handlers, and merges the user's custom Starlette/FastAPI router with the built-in meta and auth-protected routes. When `MOUNT_PREFIX` is configured it wraps the result in an outer app that keeps health and metrics endpoints at the root.
nodes.languageNotes: Application assembly happens at import time rather than in a factory function, so import order is load-bearing: `import server.api.patch` must stay first because it monkey-patches Starlette, and truststore injection runs before any TLS-using import. `ASGIBypassMiddleware` is defined conditionally inside the `MOUNT_PREFIX` branch, so it is invisible to top-level static analysis.

nodes.name: update_openapi_spec
nodes.summary: Derives the OpenAPI spec for the assembled app — using FastAPI's own generator when the user router is a FastAPI instance, otherwise falling back to a Starlette `SchemaGenerator` walk over the routes — and registers the result as the custom spec.

nodes.name: apply_middleware
nodes.summary: Wraps each route's ASGI `app` attribute in the supplied middleware stack, iterating in reverse so declaration order is preserved. Lets middleware be scoped to a bundle of routes at the mount level instead of applying globally.

nodes.name: validate_router_lifespan_hooks
nodes.summary: Guards lifespan merging by rejecting user routers that still declare legacy `on_startup`/`on_shutdown` hooks, which cannot be combined with the server's own lifespan context.

nodes.name: ASGIBypassMiddleware
nodes.summary: ASGI middleware installed only when `MOUNT_PREFIX` is set. Rewrites the request path and raw path for loopback SDK clients arriving under the `/noauth` root path so the prefixed router can still resolve them.

nodes.name: object_backend.py

nodes.name: CAREER_AGENT.md

nodes.name: 19_bulk_delete_dialog_full_paths.md

nodes.name: 21_own_agent_server.md

nodes.languageNotes: OKF bundle document: YAML frontmatter (type/title/description/tags/timestamp/status/scope/version) plus an `**Extends:**` relative link that draws the graph edge to PRD 18.

nodes.name: 23_progressive_tool_disclosure.md
nodes.summary: PRD for the chat transcript's progressive disclosure: tool calls and subagent cards stream expanded while running and auto-collapse per unit into summary rows the moment they finish, always re-expandable. Records the pure-presentation useAutoCollapse state machine, cross-message run grouping computed in ChatInterface, always-mounted collapsed bodies, and the one right-closed/down-open chevron convention.

nodes.name: 24_collapsible_threads_panel.md
nodes.summary: PRD replacing the drawer/dock split with one always-mounted Threads panel — docked on desktop, overlaying with a scrim below lg — where pinning is only a localStorage persistence preference rather than a separate rendering mode. nodes.name: 25_object_storage_artifacts.md
nodes.summary: PRD moving binary artifacts (uploads, resume and battlecard PDFs) off local disk into S3-compatible object storage — SeaweedFS locally — behind a deepagents ObjectStoreBackend mounted as CompositeBackend routes and a Starlette files API served by Python. nodes.name: 27_first_run_upload_guidance.md
nodes.summary: PRD for driving the critical first upload with actionable empty states, an in-grid upload tile, and a dismissible pulse dot — explicitly rejecting the animated coach-mark arrow on UX-research grounds. nodes.name: 28_deepagents_v07_migration.md
nodes.summary: PRD for making the career agent deepagents-0.7-native: prompt customization moves from dead monkey patches to supported middleware parameters and override-by-name instances, write_todos is restored, the silent per-turn preferences wipe is fixed with an existence probe, and write-or-replace semantics retire the custom overwrite_file tool. Records the assembled-prompt snapshot test as the tripwire for future bumps.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Agent-portable copy of the write-prd skill: instructs an AI agent to distill the current session into a PRD saved under docs/prd/, covering the 6-step workflow, the non-negotiable PRD section template, OKF frontmatter/linking rules, and the supersede procedure. Byte-identical to the .claude/ copy so both agent runtimes see the same contract.
nodes.languageNotes: Skill file format: YAML frontmatter (name + trigger-phrase description) drives skill discovery, while the body embeds a fenced markdown block as a verbatim PRD template — the fence is deliberately filled with placeholder NN_*.md link targets because the OKF graph's edge scanner also reads inside code fences.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Claude Code copy of the write-prd skill, defining how a session's work becomes a PRD in docs/prd/: mine the conversation for the why and rejected alternatives, follow the fixed section template, obey OKF frontmatter quoting and relative-link rules, and update index.md plus the regenerated viz.html.
nodes.languageNotes: Encodes OKF bundle invariants mechanically rather than by judgment — fixed frontmatter key order, per-key quoting rules (timestamp single-quoted so YAML doesn't coerce it to a datetime), a closed tag taxonomy, and reserved filenames (log.md, index.md) that must never gain frontmatter.

nodes.name: .cursorignore
nodes.summary: Cursor editor ignore-rules file that hides two generated, human-facing artifacts from the editor's AI context: the `.ua/` knowledge-graph data and the PRD-bundle viewer `docs/prd/viz.html`. Comments direct assistants to read the real source and `docs/prd/index.md` instead.

nodes.name: prompts.py
nodes.summary: Holds the five authored prompt blocks for the career agent — SYSTEM_PROMPT (5-stage workflow, coaching voice, update routing), TODO, FILE_TOOLS, EXECUTE_GUARDRAIL, and MEMORY — each wired to a supported deepagents 0.7 constructor parameter in agents.py rather than monkey-patched module constants.
nodes.languageNotes: Module-level string constants only — no functions or classes. MEMORY must keep its `{agent_memory}` placeholder: MemoryMiddleware validates it at construction and formats it at runtime. EXECUTE_GUARDRAIL is load-bearing — it blocks shell redirections that would bypass the CompositeBackend virtual routes.

nodes.name: interview-battlecard
nodes.summary: Stage-5 skill definition the main agent applies itself (no subagent) to produce the day-of one-pager: reads the tailored resume, interview-coach prep, and recon report, then emits a strict per-round JSON source-of-truth plus a rendered PDF. Specifies exact target counts per field, falsifiability rules for company facts, and the in-place update flow.
nodes.languageNotes: Frontmatter-driven Claude skill (`name` + `description`); the PDF template silently ignores unknown JSON keys, which is why the doc forbids inventing extra fields.

nodes.name: hiring-recon
nodes.summary: Skill definition for the hiring-recon subagent: given a processed CV, JD, and optional intake, run 3-5 targeted web searches across six research axes (company snapshot, financial/hiring signals, reputation, hiring team, role market context with location-bracketed salary, match analysis) and write one cited markdown report.
nodes.languageNotes: Encodes a no-fabrication contract — unfindable facts must be written as `Unknown — no public signal` rather than guessed.

nodes.name: interview-coach
nodes.summary: Skill definition for the interview-coach subagent: turns the resume, JD, intake, and recon report into a single prep doc with a reusable 60s/30s self-introduction and per-round STAR stories, questions to ask back, and watch-outs. Falls back to a 3-round taxonomy when the intake names no interview process.
nodes.languageNotes: Adds a conditional `## Triage` section when the prep timeline is under 3 days — output shape varies with an input signal.

nodes.name: resume-tailor
nodes.summary: Skill definition for the resume-tailor subagent: a 3-step workflow that picks a rendercv theme and locale, writes the tailored resume YAML, then calls `render_resume_pdf` to publish the PDF. Codifies the truth-vs-tailoring guardrail (reorder and reword, never invent) and preservation defaults for skills and source URLs.
nodes.languageNotes: Doubles as a rendercv 2.8 troubleshooting reference: a validation-error → fix catalogue, an entry-type mapping table, theme/locale allowlists, and a worked RIGHT/WRONG YAML example. The dominant failure mode it guards is an unquoted `: ` inside a string silently parsing as a YAML mapping.

Supersedes PRDs 04, 06, and 07 as the single source of truth.

nodes.name: 11_interview_battlecard_pdf.md

nodes.summary: Idempotent single-transaction Postgres migration for the Better Auth 1.6 -> 1.7 upgrade: adds and backfills the account.issuer column (credential -> local:credential, google -> accounts.google.com), aborts on unmapped providers or (issuer, accountId) collisions, then enforces NOT NULL and a unique compound index.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a PL/pgSQL DO block with RAISE EXCEPTION as a guard inside one transaction, so a failed check rolls back every schema change.

nodes.name: globals.css
nodes.summary: Global Tailwind 4 stylesheet for the Next.js app: loads the legacy tailwind.config via @config, the forms plugin and tw-animate-css, defines the light/dark theme and accent design tokens plus element base styles in @layer base, and adds shared animations (tool-running sweep, progress bar), pretty scrollbars, and word-diff highlight classes.
nodes.languageNotes: Tailwind 4 running in @config compatibility mode; element-level CSS is kept inside @layer base so utilities still win, and motion is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

nodes.name: server.ts
nodes.summary: Server-only Better Auth instance used in multi-user mode: Postgres-backed email/password auth with optional Google OAuth, plus the jwt plugin that mints short-lived JWTs (/api/auth/token, /api/auth/jwks) whose sub claim scopes backend threads, files, and memory.
nodes.languageNotes: Lazily dynamic-imported by the auth route so zero-login mode never constructs the pg Pool; nextCookies must remain the last plugin because it wraps other plugins' cookie writes.

nodes.name: config.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for the frontend runtime config module covering DEFAULT_CONFIG construction from NEXT_PUBLIC_* env vars, SSR behavior of getConfig/saveConfig without a window, and getEffectiveAgentId selection/fallback rules.
nodes.languageNotes: Because DEFAULT_CONFIG is computed at import time, each test stubs env vars with vi.stubEnv, resets modules, and dynamically re-imports a fresh copy of the module.

nodes.name: check-skill-mirrors.sh
nodes.summary: Bash guard run by pre-commit and the hygiene CI job that verifies every file under the canonical .claude/skills tree has a byte-identical mirror under .agents/skills (allowing Codex-only extras), and with --sync copies canonical files across to fix drift.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses find -print0 | sort -z with read -d '' for NUL-safe, deterministic iteration and cmp -s for byte-level comparison under set -euo pipefail.

nodes.name: json_loads
nodes.summary: Deserializes JSON via orjson, unwrapping orjson Fragments and passing already-decoded dicts through unchanged.

nodes.name: ensure_async_serde
nodes.summary: Returns the serializer as-is if it already implements AsyncSerializerProtocol, otherwise wraps it in AsyncSerializerAdapter.

tour.title: Product Overview & Workflow
tour.description: Start with the README to see what NextRole does: you upload a CV and a target job description, and a team of agents produces a tailored resume PDF, a researched interview-prep doc and a day-of battlecard. The README also introduces the second product surface, an analytics agent that answers usage questions over a ClickHouse warehouse. The agent-workflow PRD explains the staged career pipeline, and the PRD index is the map of every feature spec you can open later.

tour.title: Frontend Entry & App Shell
tour.description: The Next.js App Router page is the UI entry point and has one of the widest fan-outs in the frontend: it composes the thread list, chat, workspace and top bar inside resizable panels. The root layout wires global providers and theming, and lib/config.ts holds runtime settings such as the agent server URL. The TopBar's agent picker reads the static agents registry, which maps each LangGraph graph_id (career and analytics) to its display name, so one shell can host both agents.
tour.languageLesson: In the Next.js App Router, layout.tsx wraps every page under its folder and persists across navigations, while page.tsx is the route's leaf component. Marking a file with 'use client' moves it and its imports into the client bundle, which is needed for anything that uses hooks or browser APIs.

tour.title: Client & Chat Providers
tour.description: Below the shell, React context providers own the connection to the agent server. ClientProvider builds a memoized LangGraph SDK client and attaches the bearer token to every REST and SSE request in multi-user mode. ChatProvider exposes useChat, which wraps the @langchain/react useStream runtime, to every component, and types.ts defines the shared message, tool-call and subagent shapes, which is why it is one of the most-imported frontend files. useInterruptApprovals merges root and subagent interrupts so the UI can ask you to approve a pending tool call.
tour.languageLesson: React context plus a custom hook (createContext, a Provider component, and a useX() accessor that throws outside the provider) is the standard way to share a stateful client across a component tree without prop drilling. Keeping the hook as the only public API lets the provider change its internals freely.

tour.title: Chat Stream, Approvals & Workspace
tour.description: With the providers from Step 3 in place, ChatInterface renders the streamed conversation: ChatMessage draws each message and its grouped tool calls, and SubagentCard shows delegated subagent work with its own tool trail. When the agent wants to run a shell command, ToolApprovalInterrupt shows the arguments and lets you approve or reject it. On the right, Workspace shows the live plan, sources and generated files (CV uploads, resume PDFs, prep docs), so you see artifacts appear as the agents produce them.

tour.title: The Career Agent Core
tour.description: Now switch to the backend that the UI streams from. agents.py assembles the career agent as a DeepAgents graph and is one of the most depended-on backend files: it wires tools, subagents, skills, memory and the storage backends you will meet in Step 7. prompts.py holds the authored prompt blocks (including the five-stage workflow), each passed through a supported DeepAgents constructor parameter rather than patched in. middleware.py stamps the date, ensures the preferences memory file exists and applies per-run model overrides, and CAREER_AGENT.md is the always-loaded long-term memory that shapes behaviour across sessions.
tour.languageLesson: LangChain v1 agent middleware hooks into the model loop (before_model, wrap_model_call, wrap_tool_call), which lets cross-cutting concerns like model selection or access checks stay out of the core agent definition. The middleware list composes in order, much like ASGI middleware around a request.

tour.title: Tools, Subagents & Templates
tour.description: tools.py defines the career agent's custom LangChain tools and is among the most-imported backend modules. subagents.yaml declares the three specialist subagents the main agent delegates to (hiring-recon, resume-tailor, interview-coach), each with its own model, tool allowlist and SKILL.md playbook such as resume-tailor. execute_approval.py is the human-in-the-loop policy behind Step 4's approval panel: it auto-approves only provably read-only shell commands and pauses everything else. The Jinja battlecard template renders the final one-page-per-round PDF.

tour.title: Artifact Storage & Sandboxed Execution
tour.description: Every artifact the agents read or write lives in S3-compatible object storage (SeaweedFS locally). object_storage.py wraps the store client, object_backend.py presents it to DeepAgents as a filesystem keyed by user and area, and shell_backend.py or the E2B-protocol sandbox_backend.py runs the execute tool locally or in an isolated remote sandbox. files_api.py is mounted into the agent server and serves the list, download and upload endpoints that Step 4's Workspace uses.

tour.title: Agent Server: API & Streaming
tour.description: The agents are hosted by a self-hosted, LangGraph-compatible agent server. server.py builds the ASGI app with its middleware stack, api/__init__.py is the route table for assistants, threads, runs, store, MCP and A2A endpoints, runs.py creates and joins runs, and stream.py turns graph execution into the event stream the frontend consumes. ARCHITECTURE.md explains the two-plane design (HTTP API plus gRPC core-server) and is the best map of this package.
tour.languageLesson: Starlette/ASGI apps are built from a list of Route objects plus a middleware stack; each middleware wraps the next app callable. Server-sent events stream a long-lived HTTP response as 'event:'/'data:' lines, which is how token and step updates reach the browser without WebSockets.

tour.title: Runtime, Data Plane & Schema
tour.description: Underneath the API from Step 8, graph.py is the graph registry that loads the registered graphs (career and analytics) from their env specs. runtime_postgres provides the Postgres checkpointer, long-term store and the run queue, which dispatches queued runs to background workers. core_server is the internal gRPC data plane that owns assistant, thread, run and cron SQL. The init migration defines the tables all of this persists to, including thread, run, checkpoints and store, which the analytics pipeline later extracts from.
tour.languageLesson: LangGraph checkpointing stores a snapshot of graph state after every step keyed by thread_id, which is what makes runs resumable after an interrupt (such as a tool approval) and lets the UI reload history. The checkpoint tables in the migration are that persistence contract.

tour.title: Multi-User Authentication
tour.description: Identity starts in the frontend: better-auth runs server-side in lib/auth/server.ts, the client helper manages sessions, and SessionGate keeps the app behind sign-in when auth is enabled. On the agent server, auth/custom.py plugs a user-supplied Auth object into request handling to verify the caller, and scope.py turns that identity into per-user namespaces and object-key scopes, so each user's uploads, artifacts and memories stay isolated in the object store from Step 7.

tour.title: Analytics Pipeline: Extract & Orchestrate
tour.description: The analytics/ app turns the runtime and auth Postgres tables from Steps 9-10 into BI data. definitions.py is the Dagster code location that registers everything; assets_dlt.py defines two dlt pipelines that load runtime tables into raw_app and Better Auth tables into raw_auth in ClickHouse, and transforms.py enforces the privacy rule of shipping structure and metrics, never document bodies (whitelisted metadata, hashed emails). schedules.py runs the whole asset graph hourly.
tour.languageLesson: Dagster models pipelines as software-defined assets: each asset declares the data it produces and its upstream dependencies, and Dagster derives the lineage graph and run order from those declarations rather than from hand-written task DAGs.

tour.title: Warehouse Marts, Cube & Superset
tour.description: dbt shapes the raw ClickHouse tables into staging views and gold-layer marts: fct_run captures run reliability and latency, while fct_message prices every message against the model_prices seed to estimate LLM cost. The Cube overview view puts named metrics (active users, success rate, latency) on top of those marts, and the Superset 'NextRole Overview' dashboard bundle, the most-referenced analytics config, charts them for humans.
tour.languageLesson: This is a medallion layout: bronze (raw dlt loads), silver (dbt staging views that rename and cast), and gold (marts at a clear grain such as one row per run). dbt's ref() and source() calls build the dependency graph, so 'dbt build' runs models and their tests in the right order.

tour.title: The Analytics Agent
tour.description: The second DeepAgents graph is registered beside the career agent and answers product questions over the marts from Step 12. agents.py wires three tools from tools.py: describe_data, run_sql and create_chart. metadata.py merges dbt docs, Cube definitions and ClickHouse system facts into one data dictionary, warehouse.py enforces read-only SQL (statement classification, LIMIT injection), and ANALYTICS_AGENT.md is its always-loaded memory of the warehouse layout.

tour.title: Charts End to End
tour.description: Charts connect the analytics agent back to the UI from Step 4. charts.py validates a chart spec against query results and stores a Plotly-ready envelope, and the frontend's charts.ts mirrors that envelope as a zod schema. ChartCard renders the chart once in the chat, while InlineChart embeds a stored chart inside reports. The charts SKILL.md teaches the agent which chart kind to pick and how to embed charts in report dashboards.
tour.languageLesson: Mirroring a backend payload as a zod schema gives the frontend runtime validation plus a TypeScript type from one definition (z.infer<typeof Schema>). A malformed or older chart envelope fails safeParse and can be handled cleanly instead of crashing the renderer.

tour.title: Containers & CI
tour.description: docker-compose.yml runs the whole stack described in this tour on one machine: frontend, agent server and core-server, Postgres, Redis and SeaweedFS, plus ClickHouse, Dagster, dbt docs, Cube and Superset. The backend and analytics Dockerfiles are multi-stage uv builds. In GitHub Actions, ci.yml runs the code-quality hooks and analytics-tests.yml runs the pipeline tests, each behind a change-detection job so docs-only PRs skip heavy work without blocking required checks.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds resolve dependencies in a builder stage (here, uv syncing a locked venv) and copy only the finished venv into a slim runtime image. In Compose, one-shot init services such as object-store-init or superset-init combined with depends_on conditions order bootstrap tasks before the long-running services start.
